prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
UKIP Manifesto 2015 — Summary (ideological framing preserved)

UKIP offers a clear, costed plan to take back control of Britain’s laws, borders and money, restore democratic accountability, and make government serve the British people. By leaving the EU, cutting waste, and rebalancing spending away from vanity projects and foreign giveaways, UKIP says we can invest in frontline services without raising taxes or debt.

Core principles
- Sovereignty and democracy: Leave the EU, restore British law under a UK Bill of Rights, hold regular people-initiated referendums, and make MPs genuinely accountable through real recall and open primaries. Move to a fairer, proportional voting system.
- Controlled, fair immigration: End EU free movement, adopt an Australian-style points system, impose a five-year moratorium on unskilled immigration, count people in and out, and require five years of tax/NI before access to most benefits and non-urgent NHS care. No amnesty for illegal immigration; deport foreign criminals.
- Sound money, lower taxes, better value: Save billions by leaving the EU, cutting foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula, and trimming quangos and Westminster waste. Raise the personal allowance to ~£13,000, lift the 40% threshold to £55,000 with a new 30% band, abolish inheritance tax and the bedroom tax, and cut small business rates. Clamp down on multinational tax avoidance.
- NHS and social care first: Keep a national, free-at-point-of-use NHS; invest £12bn over five years for 8,000 more GPs, 20,000 nurses and 3,000 midwives; tackle A&E pressures with GP-led pilots; boost mental health and dementia funding; end health tourism via mandatory insurance; scrap hospital parking charges. Restore social care funding (£1.2bn/yr) and integrate health and social care.
- Jobs and small business: Prioritise British workers, enforce the minimum wage, curb late payments by large firms, improve access to finance, cut red tape from Brussels, and give SMEs a level shot at public contracts. Sensible guardrails on zero-hours abuses.
- Homes and communities: Build on brownfield first with real incentives, bring empties back into use, prioritise locals for social housing, reinvest Right to Buy receipts, protect the green belt, and restrict Help to Buy and social housing access to those with strong UK ties.
- Energy you can afford: Repeal the Climate Change Act, scrap green levies and subsidies for wind/solar while backing reliable, diverse supply—nuclear, gas (including shale with safeguards), coal, and hydro—to keep the lights on and bills down.
- Transport and infrastructure: Scrap HS2; use cameras only for safety, not revenue; oppose pay-as-you-go road charging; back UK hauliers and scrap unnecessary driver regulation.
- Law, order and borders: More frontline police, prison and border staff; zero tolerance of grooming, FGM and forced marriage; decriminalise TV-licence non-payment; modernise sentencing for cyber, trafficking and sexual crimes; prisons focused on punishment and rehabilitation.
- Defence and security: Meet and exceed 2% of GDP on defence, retain Trident, rebuild capabilities, oppose any EU army, create a Director of National Intelligence, and make active-service pay income-tax free.
- British culture and nationhood: Promote integration, protect free speech, uphold one law for all, teach British history with pride, make St George’s and St David’s Days bank holidays, and put heritage before overdevelopment.
- Farming, fishing, and countryside: Replace CAP with fair UK support focused on family farms; restore control of UK waters (200-mile EEZ), rebuild our inshore fleet, end destructive practices, improve animal welfare, and enable honest food labelling.
- Trade not aid: Cut and refocus overseas aid on clean water, vaccinations and disaster relief; close DFID and fold essential functions into the FCO. After Brexit, strike UK-led global trade deals while securing tariff-free access to the EU market.

Brexit roadmap
Hold an in/out referendum, trigger Article 50 for an orderly exit, reassert our WTO seat, agree a UK–EU free-trade deal and practical cooperation (security, health, science), and replace EU rules with British law. UKIP’s message: believe in Britain—prosperous, self-governing, secure and fair.
